objective: Schedule one deferred zero-argument callback and return an independent idempotent cancel closure.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Cancellation closures are useful UI/application building blocks.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Deferred execution and resource identity transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded nonnegative delays isolate the lesson from coercion/overflow.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Zero-delay inline invocation and cross-timer cancellation are meaningful errors.

defects: Delay domain, inline-versus-deferred behavior and callback argument/receiver scope were implicit.
No delayed-before-deadline cancellation at a nonzero point or maximum delay test existed.
Host timer cost and wall-clock timing were not distinguished.
rationale: Retain all correct timer/cancel boards. Define integer delays 0..1000, normally-returning receiver-independent tasks with no arguments, ignored callback/cancel returns, no inline execution and minimum-delay semantics. State constant wrapper work excluding host timer management/task work. Add zero-delay deferred order/exact arity, maximum-delay double cancellation and two timers where one is cancelled by an earlier separate timer. Use virtual timer evidence, not physical wall-clock precision claims. New asynchronous completion probes guard missing cancel functions so an incomplete starter yields a normal failed check rather than leaving a hidden promise unresolved.

objective: Dispatch exactly the requested sequence of numbered interval callbacks and release its own interval.

relevanceRationale.transferable: Counters, cleanup and per-instance resource ownership transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Positive delays and bounded counts keep the exercise precise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Zero-count allocation and missed cleanup risk stray callbacks.

defects: Count/delay domains, exact callback arity and no-inline rule were implicit.
A ten-call cap passed small old scenarios.
The prompt did not separate total callback work from elapsed waiting/host scheduling.
The old cleanup probe left global allocation tracking active while awaiting timers, so shuffled hidden cases could count another check's still-running interval.
rationale: Retain all correct interval programs and define times 0..1000, ms 1..1000, normally-returning tasks, exactly one 1-based number argument and no inline calls. Zero starts no interval, separate repeats keep separate state and returns are ungraded. Explain linear total wrapper dispatch count with constant retained state, excluding wait/host/task costs. Add 100 callbacks with count/sum/last/arity observations and a scoped zero-count interval-allocation probe; original cleanup tests remain. An initial 1000-tick asynchronous test passed production QuickJS but exceeded the auxiliary native VM wait limit; the final 100-tick check stays within that limit without introducing timer-stub restrictions on otherwise valid captured timer aliases. The supported 1000-count bound is established by source reading, not a claimed maximum-count native timing run. Repair the old cleanup fixture to wrap only allocations made synchronously by its own two repeat calls, restore setInterval immediately, and count excess actual firings of those intervals; it no longer depends on global cancellation hooks or includes intervals from other hidden checks. This catches a still-live interval even when learner callback effects are guarded. Captured timer aliases are not rejected merely for bypassing instrumentation.

objective: Report synchronous division once through exact error-first callback arguments and propagate callback errors unchanged.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Error-first callbacks remain present in Node interfaces.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: A small callback adapter makes the protocol concrete.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Return-versus-callback and throw propagation transfer broadly.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Finite bounded Numbers avoid unrelated coercion/overflow cases.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Double callbacks, swallowed failures and signed-zero denominators are material risks.

defects: Number domains, synchronous invocation and callback argument counts were implicit.
Swallowing a callback error passed old checks.
Serialized undefined results did not directly assert the normal undefined return.
rationale: Retain all correct implementations. Define bounded finite inputs and a lower magnitude bound for nonzero denominators, both signed zeros as errors, exact one error argument/two success arguments, no rounding, synchronous once-only invocation and ignored callback return. A callback throw propagates unchanged without retry. Add 1.005/2 precision and invocation order, negative-zero denominator and output sign, direct undefined-return predicates and original callback-thrown object identity on both branches.

objective: Count independent calls and invoke a zero-argument completion callback once synchronously on the exact threshold.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Joining a fixed number of callbacks is practical.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Threshold state and exactly-once effects transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Integer count/call bounds make behavior unambiguous.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Error/reentry must not accidentally repeat completion.

defects: Upper count/call bounds, synchronous invocation and error consumption were implicit.
A count cap of 100 passed all old cases.
No thrown-completion or callback reentry case existed.
rationale: Retain all correct boards. Define count 1..10000, up to 10000 calls, fresh independent returned functions, ignored arguments, zero-argument synchronous done and unspecified wrapper return. The threshold is consumed even if done throws. Add 10000-call boundary/freshness, original thrown object identity followed by ignored extra calls and done reentering its completed wrapper. Constant wrapper work excludes done.
